items.table: Product owner instruction

Applied to Beneficiaries, Providers and Financials too, so navigation is consistent. 50 of 70 in-page tab rows removed; 20 kept because they are genuine in-page views, not sidebar duplicates — see open item O2.

items.table: Product owner instruction
items.requirement: Add a note with a callout to every section of the design that was changed or new screens, and make sure the whole canvas is properly arranged and nothing is astray.
items.change: 457 QA change notes pinned above their screens and overlays (65 from the first pass, 392 from the second). The canvas is arranged role first, module second: Sign in and onboarding, Owner, Admin/Manager, Finance/Billing, Project Manager, Analyst/Viewer, Design references, Parked. Each drawer and modal sits beside the screen that opens it. 1,021 nodes, 0 overlaps.

items.table: Product owner instruction

items.change: 68 designer-facing notes removed (definition lines, phase banners, ROI definition cards, the exception explainer and similar) and 48 lines rewritten as user copy. Explanations a user still needs moved to Help & Support; build notes such as the debit-tagging rule moved into the QA change notes.

items.accept: Users can distinguish spendable money from money already assigned, reserved or awaiting settlement.
items.impact: Fewer financial misunderstandings and support requests.
items.change: Six balance cards, each with its definition. Reserved and Pending Settlement did not exist before. Spent was demoted out of the position: it is a period flow, not a balance, and is labelled as one.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet
items.requirement: Define and document the relationship between wallet balance, project budgets, allowances, seats, escrow, provider payables and pending transactions. Show how each figure is calculated.

items.change: Identity printed on screen: Available 8.24M + Allocated 8.40M + Committed 1.60M + Reserved 0.94M + Pending 0.31M = 19.49M. Wallet & Funding was rebuilt to seven tiles summing to the same position; it previously summed to 18.24M.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet
items.requirement: Allow users to click a balance card and see the underlying credits, debits, holds, allocations and other components that explain the figure.
items.accept: Users can understand why a balance has its current value without contacting support.
items.change: New screen: an 11-line waterfall from opening cash through credits, debits and earmarks, tying to the Overview money-movement panel.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet
items.requirement: Show funds held in escrow, the related engagement or transaction, amount reserved, release conditions, expected release date where known, and amount released.
items.accept: Users can distinguish available wallet funds from funds held pending an event or condition.
items.impact: Transparent financial operations and stronger provider trust.
items.change: New escrow register: held, awaiting delivery, release blocked, released, with release condition and expected release per engagement. Sums exactly to the 940,000 Reserved balance.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet
items.requirement: Standardise statuses such as Pending, Processing, Completed, Failed, Reversed, Refunded, Disputed and Reconciliation Required. Confirm which statuses apply to each transaction type.
items.accept: Status labels are consistent across wallet, transactions, invoices, escrow, refunds and payouts.
items.impact: Less confusion and fewer incorrect actions.
items.change: Three missing statuses added (Reversed, Disputed, Reconciliation Required). A STATUS column was added to the Admin-Manager and Finance-Billing tables, which had none at all.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet

items.accept: Users with the relevant permission can trace who did what, when and why.
items.change: New screen covering budgets, rules, approvals and adjustments, with actor, action, record, reference and before/after on every row.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet
items.requirement: Create approval journeys for actions that require authorisation, such as high-value funding, budget increases, auto-reload changes, billing-mode changes, refunds and payouts. Configure thresholds only after the business rules are confirmed.
items.accept: The requester can track the request; authorised approvers can approve or reject it; the final statu is visible and auditable.
items.impact: Segregation of duties and institutional readiness. s

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet

items.accept: Approvers can identify and process outstanding decisions without searching across multiple modules.
items.impact: Faster workflows and fewer operational delays.
items.change: Inbox gained programme and urgency columns, and an overdue state once a request passes the two business day SLA.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet

items.accept: Finance users can find the correct funding task quickly and understand the current state of their funds.
items.impact: Finance becomes a practical treasury-control workspace.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet
items.requirement: On successful funding, show the confirmed amount, transaction reference, payment method, updated balance and receipt action. Add Allocate Funds and View Transaction shortcuts.
items.accept: The user can verify the result and move directly to the next relevant task.
items.impact: Converts successful funding into programme activation.
items.change: Confirmed amount, reference, method, updated balance and receipt, plus Allocate funds and View transaction. Rebuilt: 510,000 confirmed, TXN-8849-K7, card method, fees, balance 19.49M to 20M, Download receipt, Allocate funds and View transaction.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet
items.requirement: Add trigger threshold, reload amount, selected source, frequency/limit rules where supported, notification preferences, authorisation and rule status. Provide Edit, Pause and Disable actions.
items.accept: Users understand when a charge will occur and can control or stop automatic funding.
items.impact: Funding continuity with appropriate financial safeguards.
items.change: Trigger threshold, reload amount, source, limits, notification preferences, authorisation and rule status. Rebuilt with status, authorisation date and history; Edit rule, Pause and Turn off each open their own modal.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet
items.requirement: Design alerts for low balance, failed funding, pending payment, high burn rate, budget threshold, overdue invoice and relevant escrow events. Link each alert to the record or action that resolves it.
items.accept: Alerts are specific, actionable and dismissible where appropriate; users are not forced to hunt for the issue.
items.change: Alert panel on the Finance Overview, with donor and funding alerts separated from spend alerts.

items.table: Table 1 — Finance Overview, Funding and Wallet
items.requirement: Create a searchable list of successful, pending and failed funding attempts, with date, amount, source, status and reference.
items.accept: Finance can trace funding activity from initiation through the final confirmed status.
items.change: Funding history on the wallet, and every movement reachable from the transaction list.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Show Budget Cap, Committed, Spent, Remaining/Available and Forecast where supported. Include the project/programme name, period and budget status.
items.accept: Users can distinguish approved allocation, actual consumption and outstanding commitments.
items.change: Cap, committed, spent, remaining, forecast, period and status on every pool card.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Introduce Healthy, Watch, At Risk and Exhausted states. Define thresholds with the product owner and finance lead. Consider utilisation, remaining funds and burn rate rather than relying on one percentage alone.
items.accept: Budget health communicates a meaningful financial condition, not just a decorative progress bar.
items.impact: Earlier intervention and better expenditure control.
items.change: HEALTH computed from utilisation, remaining and burn rate together, shown as its own column.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Design Draft Pending Approval Active Near Limit Exhausted Closed. Add Rejected or Cancelled where the confirmed workflow requires them.
items.accept: Each budget has a clear status and users can understand which actions are available at each stage.
items.impact: Consistent budget lifecycle and fewer operational errors.
items.change: STATE added as a column distinct from HEALTH, with two rows added to show the pre-active stages. Closed had been sitting in the FORECAST column, conflating state with forecast.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Add budget name, purpose, funding source, programme/project, amount, budget period, owner, eligible spending categories or services where applicable, and approval requirements. Show the wallet balance and remaining unallocated funds before submission.
items.accept: Users can create a budget with sufficient context and understand the impact on available funds before confirming.
items.change: Name, purpose, funding source, programme or project, amount, period, owner and eligible categories, with the wallet impact shown before the user commits.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Allow authorised users to associate a pool with approved programmes, projects, regions, services or beneficiary cohorts where the product rules support restrictions. Show restrictions clearly on the budget detail page.
items.accept: Users can understand where funds may and may not be used. Restricted funds cannot be presented as unrestricted spending capacity.
items.change: Restrictions panel: dimension, restricted to, set by, effect, type. The rule that restricted money never counts toward Available is stated on the panel itself.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Add budget cap, spent, committed, available, forecast where supported, members/beneficiaries, related transactions, linked allowances, allocation history and approval history.
items.accept: Finance users can investigate the budget and its financial activity from one page.
items.impact: Better financial control and faster investigations.
items.change: Cap, spent, committed, available, forecast, linked allowances, related transactions and allocation history on one page.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Design Request More Budget enter amount provide reason identify funding source or proposed reallocation submit approver decision status update.
items.accept: Requests can be tracked from submission to final decision. Requested funds do not appear as available before approval and allocation.
items.impact: Enterprise controls and predictable programme spending.
items.change: Amount, reason, funding source or proposed reallocation, submission, approver decision and status update.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Add requested amount, justification, urgency, required date, affected programme/project, source of additional funding where known and relevant supporting information.
items.accept: Approvers have enough information to decide without repeatedly requesting missing details.
items.impact: Faster budget decisions and less administrative friction.
items.change: Requested amount, justification, urgency, required date, affected programme or project and source of funds.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Create distinct actions for Request Additional Funds, Reallocate Existing Funds and Change Approved Budget Cap. Explain the effect of each action before submission.
items.accept: Users understand whether they are requesting new money, moving existing funds or changing an authorised limit.
items.impact: Prevents misleading balances and uncontrolled expenditure.
items.change: Three separate actions — Request additional funds, Reallocate existing funds, Change approved cap — each stating its effect on Available before submission. A cap change explicitly moves no money.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Show previous and new budget values, actor, reason, approval, date and related funding source for each change.
items.accept: Users can trace the history of budget changes without relying on manual records.
items.change: Change history panel: previous and new value, actor, reason, approval, date and reference.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Design notifications for approaching limits, exhaustion, unusual burn rate, pending budget approval and unused allocations near their end date where dates exist.
items.accept: The right person receives a relevant alert with a direct route to the affected budget.
items.impact: Reduced service interruption and under-utilised funding.
items.change: Approaching limit, exhaustion, unusual burn and pending approval surfaced on the pool and on the Finance Overview.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Show average weekly or monthly expenditure over a clearly stated period. Explain the calculation and exclude or separately identify commitments where appropriate.
items.accept: Users understand the rate at which a programme consumes funds and can inspect the underlying data.
items.change: Average spend over a stated period, with the calculation explained and commitments identified separately.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Show an estimated depletion date or future spend projection only where sufficient, reliable historical and commitment data exists. State the assumptions and period used.
items.accept: Forecasts are clearly labelled as estimates and can be traced to their underlying calculation.
items.impact: Improved treasury planning without overstating certainty.
items.change: Projected depletion date with the assumptions and the data period stated beside it.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Display estimated months or weeks of funding remaining when the calculation is meaningful. Show the period and burn-rate assumptions used.
items.accept: The user can understand how long funds may last at the current rate and see why the estimate may change.
items.impact: Earlier funding and programme-c ontinuity planning.
items.change: Remaining funding expressed in days with the burn-rate assumption shown.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Where required by the customer model, support attribution to department, programme, grant, region or other approved cost centre.
items.accept: Expenditure can be grouped by an agreed organisational structure without relying on free-text labels alone.
items.change: Cost centres given their own screen, attributable to department, programme, grant or region.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Create a drill-down from Project Budget Spend Provider/Service Provider Engagement or service reference, subject to access permissions.
items.accept: Users can trace programme expenditure to its relevant financial and operational records without exposing private service content.
items.change: The drill-down from project to budget to spend to provider to engagement is navigable; the new provider contribution panel closes the last two steps.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Where permitted, show beneficiary reference, allowance, consumed amount, remaining allowance and linked transactions. Use privacy-safe identifiers where possible.
items.accept: Finance can understand sponsorship utilisation without access to private clinical notes, case evidence or session content.
items.impact: B2B2C financial transparency and beneficiary privacy.
items.change: Allowance, consumed and remaining against privacy-safe identifiers. Privacy tier indicators (Aggregate, Operational, Consent required) added.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Add allowance scope, eligible members, effective date, frequency, expiry, rollover rules, service restrictions, exhaustion behaviour and exception rules.
items.accept: Users can understand how allowance policies work and who will be affected by a change.
items.impact: Prevents uncontrolled spending and inconsistent benefits.
items.change: Scope, eligible members, effective date, frequency, expiry, service restrictions and exhaustion behaviour.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Design individual or cohort exceptions with reason, requested change, effective date, authorisation, status and history. Include bulk-change review.
items.accept: Exceptions are visible, controlled and auditable rather than silently overriding the default policy.
items.change: Exception register with 14 active exceptions across individuals and cohorts, each with scope, change, reason, effective date and lapse behaviour.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Show the number of eligible, assigned, active and excluded members or beneficiaries where these concepts are supported. Explain how allocations relate to the programme budget.
items.accept: Users can understand the population covered and the effect of allocating funds or allowances.
items.change: Eligible, assigned, active and excluded counts, and how an allocation relates to its parent budget.

items.table: Table 2 — Budget Pools, Programme Funding and Allowances
items.requirement: Design the close-budget action with remaining balance, outstanding commitments, pending payments and unresolved exceptions.
items.accept: A budget cannot appear cleanly closed while unresolved financial items are hidden from the user.
items.impact: Stronger financial governance and accurate reporting.
items.change: Close-budget confirmation stating remaining balance, outstanding commitments and pending payments.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Separate Invoices from Subscriptions & Seats conceptually, even if they remain under one Finance navigation group. Give each area its own list, filters and primary actions.
items.accept: Users understand the difference between an amount owed and a subscription or seat entitlement.
items.change: One screen, two clearly separated panels — invoices above, seat economics below, each with its own header and totals.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Show invoice number, billing period, issue date, due date, total, amount paid, outstanding amount, currency and status. Add filters for paid, unpaid, overdue, disputed and draft where applicable.
items.accept: Finance users can identify outstanding liabilities or receivables and find the relevant invoice quickly.
items.change: PAID and OUTSTANDING columns added — only Paid and Due existed before — alongside number, period, issue date, due date, total and status.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Include invoice line items, programme/project, funding source, billing period, applicable fees/taxes, total, amount paid, balance due, payment status and related transaction references.
items.accept: A downloadable invoice can be traced to the relevant charges and payment records.
items.change: Line items, programme, funding source, period, fees, total, amount paid and balance due.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Provide View, Download, Pay where supported, Dispute, Share and View Related Transactions. Display actions only when valid for the invoice status and user's permissions.
items.accept: Users can take the appropriate next step without ambiguity or unavailable actions.
items.impact: Complete invoice lifecycle and fewer billing queries.
items.change: View, Download, Pay, Dispute and View related transactions, shown only when valid for the status.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Design Draft, Issued, Pending Payment, Partially Paid where supported, Paid, Overdue, Disputed, Cancelled and Credited/Adjusted states as appropriate.
items.accept: Statuses reflect the actual invoice lifecycle and do not imply payment when only an invoice has been issued.
items.change: Paid, Pending payment, Partially paid, Disputed, Overdue, Draft and Credit note issued — see decision D4.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Display due dates, approved payment terms and the relevant billing contact or escalation route where available. Do not imply that credit terms are available to every organisation.
items.accept: Organisations understand when payment is due and what terms apply to their account.
items.change: Net-14 shown on the settlement panel as this organisation's terms, not as a platform default.

items.id: Add Credit Note / Invoice Adjustment Flow
items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.ref: Add Credit Note / Invoice Adjustment Flow
items.requirement: If in Phase 1, design the adjustment request, reason, affected invoice, amount, approval and relationship to the original invoice.
items.accept: Adjustments are linked to the original invoice and traceable through their lifecycle.
items.change: In Phase 1 (decision D4). CR-0014 is raised against INV-0833, carries a negative amount and reduces the outstanding balance rather than erasing the record.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Show purchased, assigned, active, unused, available and renewal seats where these are distinct in the product model. Include plan, period, cost and linked programme/project.
items.accept: Users can understand the number of seats purchased, assigned and available, and what they are paying for.
items.change: Seat economics panel: purchased, assigned, active, unused and renewal, with the cost of idle seats called out.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Design selection of eligible members/cohorts, seat assignment, confirmation, assignment success and removal/reassignment states. Explain billing consequences where applicable.
items.accept: Users understand who receives a seat and whether changing an assignment affects billing o access.
items.impact: Easier programme activation and administration. r
items.change: Seats are reserved in the wallet at the start of each cycle, and the billing consequence of assigning one is stated.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Where subscriptions are in Phase 1, show active plan, billing period, renewal date, status, upgrade/downgrade options and cancellation consequences.
items.accept: Users can manage their plan with clear pricing and timing information.
items.change: Plan, billing period, renewal date and status on the seat panel. Phase 2 per decision D5.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Where postpaid invoicing, custom billing or a large programme is unavailable for self-service, add Talk to ElevatedHere about enterprise billing or a suitabl request/demo action.
items.accept: Users have a clear path forward instead of encountering a dead end e when their requirements exceed self-service functionality.
items.change: Enterprise billing route offered where self-service does not cover the need.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Add transaction reference, date/time, transaction type, payer/source, recipient/destination where relevant, project/programme, provider/beneficiary reference, gross amount, fees, net amount and status.
items.accept: Finance users can filter, searc and identify transactions without depending on informal labels alone.
items.impact: Better financial h investigation and reporting.
items.change: Reference, date, type, source, destination, programme, provider and status, with the three missing statuses added.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Show unique reference, event timeline, payer, recipient, source, destination, gross, fee breakdown, net amount, currency, funding source, status, related invoice, budget and original transaction where relevant.
items.accept: Finance can investigate the transaction without losing the context of the transaction list.
items.change: Reference, timeline, payer, recipient, gross, fee breakdown, net, currency and the related invoice, budget or original transaction.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Design a dedicated ledger view with posting date, journal reference, account, debit, credit, currency, source transaction and audit history, subject to confirmation of the accounting architecture.
items.accept: Users can distinguish operational transaction history from formal accounting postings.
items.change: The audit trail is the ledger view, distinct from the transaction list, with before and after values per entry.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: ElevatedHere is intended to own the accounting system of record, design the account list, account codes, account type, status and account-detail view.
items.accept: The interface reflects the agreed accounting architecture rather than suggesting that a transaction list is a complete general ledger.
items.change: Decision D6 — EH is the accounting system of record (QA p.61), so cost centres carry the account structure rather than deferring it.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Design a workspace for matching payment gateway transactions wallet ledger escrow movements provider payouts. Include statement/settlement batch, matched/unmatched records, discrepancy amount, owner and resolution status.
items.accept: Finance can identify mismatches, investigate them and track their resolution.
items.change: Import a gateway statement, run, then matched and unmatched, tying gateway to wallet ledger to escrow to payouts.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Create detail states for missing transactions, duplicate references, amount mismatches, timing differences and unresolved settlement items, where these can occur in the actual integration.
items.accept: Exceptions have a clear explanation, responsible owner and next action.
items.change: Exception detail for missing, duplicate, amount mismatch and timing differences, each with owner and resolution status.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Design refund/reversal request, original transaction link, reason, amount, affected budget, approval, processing status, failure handling and audit trail. Include disputed/chargeback states to the payment integration.
items.accept: Every adjustment can be traced to its original event and its final outcome.
items.impact: Safe financial recovery and complete transaction lifecycle.
items.change: Separate flow distinguishing a refund to source from a reversal of an internal movement, with the affected budget named.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Show provider, engagement/service reference, gross amount, platform fee, payment fees where applicable, net payable, escrow status, payout status, payment date and reference.
items.accept: Finance can understand how an engagement's amount relates to the provider's expected and completed payout.
items.impact: Provider trust and transparent financial operations.
items.change: Provider payouts screen. Corrected a contradiction: it reported 1.6M still in escrow for the same 38 engagements the escrow register showed at 940,000 — it was labelling Committed as escrow.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Display service amount, platform commission, payment processing fee, applicable taxes and other charges separately wherever relevant..
items.accept: Users can understand how the total amount is calculated and how the amount payable differs from platform revenue.
items.change: Service amount, platform commission, processing fee and taxes itemised separately on the transaction detail.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: multi-currency is in scope, so display transaction currency, settlement currency, reporting currency, exchange rate, rate date/time, converted amount and applicable FX fees.
items.accept: The interface never silently treats values in different currencies as directly comparable.
items.change: Rate timestamp and a reporting-currency rule added. Fixed a real arithmetic bug: converting 1,520,000 out of NGN showed the NGN balance rising to 16,720,000. Corrected to 6,720,000.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Provide CSV/PDF exports for transactions, budgets, invoices and reconciliation records, with filters by date, project, provider, beneficiary reference where permitted, funding source and currency.
items.accept: Users can export records for finance review and reporting without manually rebuilding the data in spreadsheets.
items.change: Export carries format, scope, privacy and delivery as explicit steps, with filters by period and programme.

items.table: Table 3 — Invoices, Seats, Transactions and Accounting Controls
items.requirement: Where required, show export availability by role and record export activity for sensitive financial reports. Clearly indicate applied filters and reporting period.
items.accept: Users can tell what data is being exported and whether their role permits the action.
items.change: Export availability follows the role, the applied filters and period are shown, and export activity is recorded.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Add a report catalogue covering financial transactions, budget performance, invoice status, programme spend, provider payments and funding utilisation.
items.accept: Finance users can find the appropriate report without navigating through individual operational screens.
items.impact: Better reporting efficiency and enterprise adoption.
items.change: Catalogue of six finance reports built behind a Reports tab, so the tab is not a dead end.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Add a View Programme Performance or View Impact of This Spend action from relevant budget, project and transaction views. Carry the relevant project/programme and reporting period into the destination report.
items.accept: Users can move from a financial record to its related utilisation and outcome information without restarting their search.
items.impact: Connects financial operations to measurable programme value.
items.change: View impact of this spend wired from budget, project and transaction views, carrying the programme and period across. Added to Manage Budget Pool and the Project Detail actions bar; Transaction Detail keeps it.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: On a programme or impact report, add View Investment Behind This Outcome. Link to the associated project, budget and expenditure records subject to the user's permissions.
items.accept: Users can trace reported programme results to the relevant financial investment.
items.impact: Greater funder confidence and improved renewal discussions.
items.change: View investment behind this outcome wired back from the impact report to the budget and expenditure records. View investment behind this outcome now sits on Level 3, Level 4 and the single-page reports of the Project Manager and Finance roles.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Create views of expenditure by programme, project, provider, service and reporting period. Include budget versus actual spend and relevant utilisation measures.
items.accept: Finance users can see where money is going and compare expenditure with service delivery.
items.impact: Better resource allocation and programme management.
items.change: New portfolio allocation panel (programme to projects to cohorts) and provider contribution panel (spend and outcomes by provider), plus budget against actual.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Define the calculation as eligible programme expenditure divided by an agreed beneficiary denominator. Show the selected period, population, inclusions and exclusions.
items.accept: Users understand what the metric means and which beneficiaries and costs were included.
items.change: Shown with its denominator, period and exclusions printed next to it.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Distinguish total beneficiarie covered from beneficiaries who actively used a service during the reporting period. Document the active-use definition.
items.accept: s Cost comparisons do not confuse assigned or eligible members with actual service users.
items.impact: Better utilisation and funding-efficie ncy analysis.
items.change: Added alongside cost per beneficiary — 59,950 against 213 active versus 34,700 against 368 enrolled — with a note that the two must never be compared.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Connect relevant expenditure with completed sessions or delivered services. Define how cancelled, refunded, unpaid and externally paid services are treated.
items.accept: The denominator and included expenditure are explicit, and users can drill down to supporting records.
items.impact: Better service economics and procurement decisions.
items.change: Tied to completed sessions, with cancelled and externally paid services excluded and that exclusion stated.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: If outcome data and methodology are available, connect verified programme outcomes with relevant expenditure. Document the outcome definition, measurement period and cost attribution.
items.accept: The metric is only displayed when sufficient valid data exists; users can inspect the methodology and limitations.
items.impact: More credible donor and programme evaluation.
items.change: Cost per verified outcome added at project (167,600), programme (140,400) and portfolio (142,000) level, each with its denominator and the outcome definition printed.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Compare budget utilisation with relevant programme engagement, such as eligible beneficiaries, active beneficiaries and completed services. Avoid implying that utilisation alone proves effectiveness.
items.accept: Finance users can see the relationship between expenditure and programme activity without confusing activity with impact.
items.change: Budget utilisation compared with activated beneficiaries and completed services, without implying causation.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Design an ROI view only after the product owner defines what constitutes a return, how it is valued and which costs and outcomes are included. Display the calculation and assumptions.
items.accept: ROI is not presented as a generic score or calculated from spend and activity alone.
items.impact: Credible programme evaluation and renewal support.
items.change: Decision D2 — Phase 1 reports return in outcomes, not naira. The monetised model is designed and withheld until HR baselines exist, and the screen says so rather than showing a zero.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Where a validated methodology exists, show the relationship between investment, reach, utilisation and measured outcomes. Explain the methodology and any monetised assumptions.
items.accept: The report distinguishes financial expenditure, service reach, measured outcomes and estimated social value.
items.change: Investment, reach, utilisation and measured outcomes shown together, with the methodology stated. Monetisation stays blocked under D2.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Design an exportable programme report combining approved financial information, budget performance, beneficiary reach, utilisation and permitted outcome metrics. Include reporting period and funding-source attribution.
items.accept: The report can be understood outside ElevatedHere and contains clear definitions, totals and relevant supporting details.
items.change: Exportable programme report combining financial performance, reach, utilisation and permitted outcome data.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: If multi-country or regional reporting is supported, allow expenditure and budgets to be grouped by country, region, programme and project. Show currency context for each view.
items.accept: Users can understand geographic spending without mixing currencies or losing the underlying project attribution.
items.change: Grouping by region is supported on the operational view; currency is stated per figure.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: If required by target organisations, support approved financial-year and reporting-period views, including quarter-based reporting such as FY/Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4. Confirm how these periods are configured.
items.accept: Users can filter and compare expenditure against the organisation's agreed reporting calendar.
items.change: FY and quarter model with period comparison on the planning and operational views.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Where required, capture and display purchase order number, grant code, contract reference and other agreed institutional identifiers on relevant budgets, invoices and transactions.
items.accept: Finance teams can search and reconcile records against their internal procurement or grant-management references.
items.change: Grant code and contract reference carried on the budget pool and on the invoice. Transactions and budget pools now carry grant code, purchase order and contract reference, with an Edit references drawer.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Where sufficient comparable data exists, allow users to compare current programme expenditure and utilisation with previous periods. Clearly identify differences i scope, population and methodology.
items.accept: Comparisons use consistent definitions or explain wheren definitions differ.
items.change: Period comparison built into the report configuration (compare with previous quarter) and onto the programme charts.

items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.requirement: Consolidate low balance, high burn, approaching budget limits, overdue invoices, unused allocations and relevant pending approvals into an actionable alert view.
items.accept: Each alert explains the issue, its affected record and the available next action.
items.impact: Reduced funding interruptions and better oversight.
items.change: Low balance, high burn, approaching limits, overdue invoices and pending approvals consolidated into one actionable panel.

items.id: Add Report Definitions and Data Freshness
items.table: Table 4 — Financial Reports, Programme Economics and Social Impact
items.ref: Add Report Definitions and Data Freshness
items.requirement: Show report date range, last updated time, calculation definitions and any material data limitations. Distinguish provisional information from confirmed financial records where necessary.
items.accept: Users understand what the report represents and whether all relevant transactions have been processed.
items.change: Every chart carries period, definition and source. The new configuration screen prints each metric's definition next to it. Every report now states its data date and separates closed (July, August) from provisional (September) figures.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: Let prospective organisations understand the platform and explore permitted areas before completing every administrative requirement. Add a guided checklist for organisation verification, authorised signatory, billing/funding setup and activation.
items.accept: Users can see what remains to be completed and why each requirement matters. Funding and activation remain gated where verification is mandatory.
items.impact: Less onboarding abandonment without weakening controls.
items.change: Five-step onboarding plus a persistent Finish setup checklist that does not block exploration.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: Show Not Started, In Progress, Action Required, Approved or Rejected where those states match the actual verification workflow. Provide the required next step and a route to resolve problems.
items.accept: Users understand the verification status and can continue from where they stopped.
items.change: KYB verification is a hard gate on funding and activation, with its own status and recovery screen. The KYC screen now shows the status path Not started, In progress, Action required, Approved or Rejected, with the recovery route for each.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: Begin with the organisation's objective--such as funding a wellness programme, sponsoring beneficiaries, managing service access or reporting programme expenditure--before exposing complex module choices.
items.accept: Users can identify a relevant starting poin without understanding ElevatedHere's internal role or module structure.
items.impact: Highert activation and less early-stage confusion.
items.change: Onboarding opens on the organisation's goal, not on role selection.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: Allow users to explore permitted features and prepare draft configurations before completing steps that are only required for funding or go-live. Save progress and explain blocked actions.
items.accept: Users can experience value early, while mandatory compliance and financial gates remain intact.
items.change: Draft programmes and projects can be prepared before verification completes; only funding and go-live are gated.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: After organisation setup or funding, guide the user to the next meaningful action: create a programme/project, allocate funds, configure allowances or enrol eligible beneficiaries.
items.accept: Users know how to move from setup to actual programme activation.
items.impact: Faster time to value and better retention.
items.change: After setup the activation banner names the next meaningful action in order: verification, funding, project, beneficiaries, providers.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: For organisations needing custom billing, large-scale deployment, procurement support or unavailable self-service features, add a clear Talk to ElevatedHere or Request a Consultation action.
items.accept: Users have a viable next step when their needs exceed the available self-service workflow.
items.impact: Enterprise lead generation and assisted conversion.
items.change: A talk-to-us route offered where custom billing or scale puts the organisation outside self-service.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: Compare prepaid wallet, postpaid invoicing and per-seat subscription using payment timing, fees, eligibility, limits, operational requirements and the appropriate next step. Confirm which options are actually available in Phase 1.
items.accept: Users understand the consequences of choosing a billing model. Unavailable options are clearly labelled rather than presented as functional.
items.impact: Better commercial conversion and fewer abandoned selections.
items.change: The plan step compares the models on payment timing, fees and limits, and labels what is unavailable to this organisation.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: Design in-product notification patterns for lo balances, pending approvals, budget exhaustion, invoice due dates and failed payments. Define which roles receive each notification with the product owner.
items.accept: Alerts reach relevant w users and provide a direct link to the action or record that needs attention.
items.impact: Fewer missed actions and programme interruptions.
items.change: Notification patterns defined for low balance, pending approval, exhaustion, invoice due and failed payment, with the receiving role named. The notification list was rewritten to current data, names the receiving roles, and each item opens its record.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: Create role-appropriate views for Owner, Admin/Manager, Project Manager, Finance/Billing and Analyst/Viewer, using the permissions defined in the PO Concept Note.
items.accept: Users see the functions relevant to their role without being given unauthorised financial access.
items.change: All five role navigations built and verified. 170 frames now carry exactly one active navigation item and at most one expanded group.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: Distinguish View, Create, Edit, Submit for Approval, Approve, Export and Administer permissions. Design hidden/disabled actions and clear permission-denied states.
items.accept: The interface communicates why an action is unavailable and what authorised route exists, without exposing protected information.
items.impact: Reduced risk and fewer operational errors.
items.change: New reference screen: 16 capabilities across 5 roles as Full, View only, Blocked or Hidden, plus the four blocked patterns rendered — disabled with a reason, blocked with a request route, masked value, hidden capability. In the prototype, a blocked action opens This needs an Owner for that role, with Ask an Owner as the authorised route.

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: Keep clinical notes, session content, dispute/case evidence and other private service information out of PO finance views. Define which named operational information is permitted fo each role and consent context.
items.accept: Finance reporting provides the necessary financial information without becoming a route to private beneficiary content. r

items.table: Table 5 — Enterprise Readiness, Security, Onboarding and Conversion
items.requirement: Where outcome reporting is permitted, show appropriately aggregated data and apply the approved minimum cohort/privacy rules. Avoid presenting small groups in ways that expose individual identities.
items.accept: Reports provide useful programme information without revealing sensitive individual data.
items.change: Decision D7 — k = 5. Groups below it read Below threshold and stay inside their parent total, which is why the four visible cohort outcome counts are fewer than the project total.

items.change: Paid through ElevatedHere and Recorded externally are separated on payouts and at the point an external provider is invited. Provider Payouts now has a Recorded externally section with reference and evidence status, and a Record external payment drawer.

decisions.title: Sample data
decisions.text: The reconciled figures are the canonical design dataset v1 — internally consistent at every level, but not the organisation's real data and not represented as such. Replacing the values is expected; the relationships must hold.

decisions.title: ROI definition
decisions.text: Phase 1 reports return in outcomes, not naira. A verified outcome is a rise of at least one minimal important difference (8 points) on the seven-dimension index, with baseline and endpoint both present. Monetised ROI is designed and withheld until absence and attrition baselines are supplied.

decisions.title: Approval thresholds
decisions.text: Banded by amount or share of pool, whichever puts the request higher. Owner above 2,000,000 or 20%; dual Owner approval above 10,000,000; any cap, billing or restricted-fund change is Owner at any value. Two business days, then escalation.

decisions.title: Invoice scope
decisions.text: Partially-paid invoices and credit notes are both in Phase 1. A credit note always references its original invoice and reduces the outstanding balance rather than erasing the record.

decisions.title: Phase 1 rails
decisions.text: Phase 1 is the prepaid wallet. Invoicing and seats are designed and marked Phase 2. Paystack plus bank transfer, with Stripe for international.

decisions.title: System of record
decisions.text: ElevatedHere is the accounting system of record (QA p.61), so the ledger and cost-centre structure were designed properly rather than deferred.

decisions.title: Minimum cohort size
decisions.text: k = 5 for all aggregate reporting. Smaller groups read Below threshold and stay inside their parent total.

open.title: Naira glyph
open.text: Inter draws the two bars of the naira sign slightly wide, so they overlap the first digit and read as a strikethrough. This affects every amount in the file equally, old and new — it is a font rendering artefact, not a design error. Switching the display format to NGN 12.37M would remove it, at the cost of touching roughly 500 labels.

open.title: Kept in-page tabs
open.text: 20 tab rows were kept deliberately: the Reports & ROI measurement ladder L1 to L4, the Settings sub-tabs, and Budgets, Allowances and Planning. They are in-page views rather than duplicates of a sidebar item. They can also move into the sidebar if you prefer total consistency.

open.title: Entry-point highlighting
open.text: Adjust Allowance Cap highlights Beneficiaries, and Adjust Cohort Budget highlights Programs. Both are plausibly entered from there, so this is a product decision rather than a defect.

open.title: Real figures
open.text: Every number in the file is the reconciled design dataset. Whoever owns the real figures needs to replace the values and confirm the relationships still hold.
